Q: How booking system works here? A:

Most booking systems hold the seats once they're requested by the first person to ask. The hold is maintained for some period, perhaps 15 minutes, to allow the transaction to complete.

The systems use some sort of atomic operation, or mutex, or other locking system to ensure only one person holds the seats.

Someone will always be first, even if it's by seconds, or milliseconds.

Q: How do you display an image from s3 on a website? A:

An image stored in Amazon S3 can be included in a web page by using a normal <img> tag.

The URL to use is shown in the Amazon S3 console, but it would be something like:

http://BUCKETNAME.s3-REGION.amazonaws.com/folder/image.jpg

For example:

http://my-images.s3-ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/logos/foo.jpg

The object must be publicly accessible. This can be done in a few ways:

  • The object itself can be marked as public, or
  • A Bucket Policy on the bucket can designate the whole bucket, or a part of the bucket, as being public or
  • The URL can be augmented with an Amazon S3 pre-signed URLs, which provides temporary access to a private object. This method is great for providing access to private images to a specific user.

Q: How can i fix the Position_stack function that does not work in R? A:

For this particular case you can avoid position_stack() and just set x = col_B/2 inside aes of geom_text(). This won't work for actual stacked bar charts of course.

So the code would look something like

ggplot2::ggplot(data_df, aes(y = col_A, x = col_B)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "lightgrey") +
  geom_text(aes(label = col_B, x = col_B/2),
            color = "black"
  ) +
  theme_light() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray", fill = NA),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
